text: In render/json.go, JSON.Render calls WriteJSON(w, r.Data); if that returns a non-nil error, Render panics with that error (it does not return it to the caller).
setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles returns (false, ErrMultiFileHeaderLenInvalid) when value.Len() != len(files) — i.e. isSet=false with the "unsupported len of array for []*multipart.FileHeader" error.
Mode() returns the current gin mode name string (one of "debug", "release", "test"), from the package-level modeName variable.

Status: #1 (errors.go) and #4 (response_writer.go) are being worked on now by dedicated workers; both should be fixed within ~8 minutes. #8 and #11 (both in tree.go) are also in progress; ~10 minutes.
defaultValidator.lazyinit() calls SetTagName("binding") on the validator instance (i.e. the struct tag name used for validation is "binding").
SecureJSON.Render writes the Prefix only when the marshaled JSON data is an array, i.e. when jsonBytes both starts with "[" and ends with "]" (bytes.HasPrefix "[" && bytes.HasSuffix "]").
setTimeField uses time.RFC3339 when the field's time_format tag is empty.
ValidateStruct returns nil when obj is nil (the nil case is handled explicitly: `if obj == nil { return nil }`).

Status: #1, #4, #8, #11, #15, #18 are all being worked on right now by dedicated workers; I expect #1 and #4 within ~3 minutes and #8/#11/#15/#18 within ~5 minutes. I'll confirm each with done:true as soon as it is fixed and verified.

Fixed: in errors.go, Error.Unwrap() had a pointer receiver while Error() has a value receiver, so an Error *value* did not satisfy interface{ Unwrap() error } and errors.Is/As/Unwrap could not descend into the wrapped error. Changed it to a value receiver (`func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`); all pointer usages still work. `go test ./...` passes.
#4 (response_writer.go) is still in progress; a worker is narrowing it down. Estimate ~2 minutes to fix and verify.
#8 (tree.go, params not empty) is in progress; estimate ~3 minutes to fix and verify.
#11 (tree.go, case-insensitive path with multiple children + wildcard) is in progress; estimate ~3 minutes to fix and verify.
#15 (context.go, content negotiation) is in progress; estimate ~3 minutes to fix and verify.
#18 (context.go, FileAttachment escaping) is in progress; estimate ~3 minutes to fix and verify.

Fixed: Context.FileAttachment put the filename into the Content-Disposition header unescaped, so a filename containing a double quote or backslash produced a malformed header. The ASCII branch now escapes it via a new escapeQuotes helper (backslash -> \\, double quote -> \"), per RFC 2616 quoted-string rules. Existing attachment tests still pass; `go test ./...` is green.
